definition: A Policy selects an existing strategy identity by evaluating declared Rules against explicit typed inputs; selection never executes the strategy.
signature: Closed fields: schema_version, ontology_policy, inputs, cases, default_target. Ordered cases contain target and rule; each rule contains selector and arguments of parameter/value bindings. Repeated target or Rule occurrences remain ordered cases.
semantics: Validate all input facts, evaluate cases in source order until the first true Rule, then return that target; otherwise return the default. Only evaluated case arguments are computed. Rules are separate checked modules, never duplicated as inline Policy predicates.
relationships: Existing applies edges exactly cover the distinct case/default Operation or Calculation targets, with canonical scope restrictions. Rule references are value-level dependencies, not fabricated applies or enforces edges.
binding: Bind same-graph source evidence, Rule closure/artifact identities, typed input and argument contracts, strategy catalogue kind/content and digest, exact numeric profile and provider bytes in one immutable descriptor.
effects: No IO, ambient facts, reference lookup, target import/execution, invariant construction or caller mutation. Return a typed strategy selector identity, not a Boolean or executable object.
compatibility: Preserve v1 default behavior. New configured Policy requires v2; explicit migration requires caller-provided Rule selectors and ontology names and rejects ambiguous/coercive legacy comparisons. No implicit Rule registration or graph mutation.
verification: Native TypeScript and declarations, independent source observation, complete result consumption, changed Rule behavior, ordered cases, current catalogue membership and compiling semantic/effect mutation controls.
profile_boundary: The configured effect-free strategy profile requires nonempty explicit inputs and at least two distinct selectable target identities. These necessary checks do not prove branch reachability or semantic input sensitivity; independent behavioral witnesses remain required.
